clues.text: A decree from Caesar Augustus called for one across the whole empire, so everyone went to his own town.
When King David ordered one from Dan to Beersheba, Joab asked him why he wanted such a thing.
When the Israelites were numbered, each man twenty or older paid half a shekel, rich no more and poor no less.
In the Wilderness of Sinai, Moses listed Israel's men able to serve in the army, and they totaled 603,550.
God told Moses to leave the tribe of Levi out of this one and set them over the tabernacle instead.
God said all twenty or older who were listed in it would fall in the wilderness, except Caleb and Joshua.
Gamaliel told the Sanhedrin that Judas the Galilean drew followers in the days of this, then perished.
